extracted.intended_audience: newspaper reporters and journalism students (reporters, editors, journalism trainees)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting and writing miscellaneous local-city news items and entertaining local features (schools, libraries, museums, parks, municipal business, small incidents). Emphasizes purpose, accuracy, treatment, and techniques for making such stories attractive and useful to citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: There remain several forms of city news that require separate consideration: timely information in schools, public libraries, museums, parks, and various departments of city government; real estate, building, manufacturing, and business matters; and many little incidents in the daily life of every city that can be written up as entertaining stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual lists these subjects explicitly as belonging to the 'miscellaneous local news' category and implies the reporter should look for such items distinct from other story classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — informational local stories
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim in one class of these local stories is to furnish timely, significant information in attractive form concerning public institutions and business activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize timely, significant facts about institutions supported by public money because such information should interest every citizen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — entertaining local features
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the other class is to entertain the reader with little glimpses of the life of the city.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These stories need not be of vital importance but should be pleasantly entertaining while still truthful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive journalism objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive journalism undertakes to stimulate the interest of every citizen in municipal affairs and in public institutions by putting prominently before him from time to time significant information about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place significant information prominently and use reporting to encourage civic engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utmost accuracy and truthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: The utmost accuracy in presenting information of public affairs and business matters ... is absolutely essential. It is important to maintain the same standard of truthfulness in writing entertaining feature stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A newspaper cannot present anything in its news columns that is not true; fictitious details are no more justifiable in feature stories than in news stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment — make stories attractive in form and style
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to interest the average reader in news of various municipal activities it is necessary to make the stories attractive in form and style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use striking openings, clear organization, and engaging prose to hold readers' attention even for institutional or business topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead technique — striking facts, figures or unusual statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Striking facts and figures or unusual statements, featured at the beginning, catch the reader's eye and lead him to read the story as long as its subject matter and style interest him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: the story 'Public Schools Open' (uses startling army comparisons) and stories beginning with unusual statements like 'School for Backward Children' and 'New Feature in Manufacturing.' Use prominent, attention-grabbing information up front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective use of statistics and comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective use of statistics and comparisons is necessary to make municipal stories vivid and demonstrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text points to 'Public Schools Open' as an example where statistics and comparisons successfully emphasize scale and importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature storytelling devices (style/technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since there is practically no news interest in entertaining feature stories, the reader's attention is attracted and held by the way in which the story is told. Narrative and descriptive beginnings, conversation, suspense, humor and other devices used in short stories and novels are well adapted to these news stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt narrative/descriptive leads, use direct conversation, build suspense, and employ humor where appropriate — techniques borrowed from fiction to enliven human-interest sketches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find human-interest incidents in everyday locales
rubrics_metrics.description: Hotels, railroad stations, docks, and street cars are frequently the scenes of little comedies and tragedies that the reporter with keen insight into human life and with ability to portray them, turns into readable sketches. Animals no less than persons may be the central figures in these stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert for small, everyday incidents and vivid characters/animals; these can be developed into entertaining local sketches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize public-money-supported institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities supported by public money, these institutions should be of interest to every citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give prominence to reporting on publicly funded institutions (schools, libraries, museums, parks, municipal departments) because they affect the public and deserve coverage.
